_meta.source: hand-curated seed; replaced by scraper/build_bundle.py output
_meta.format: country-iso2 -> { name, plonkit_slug, identify[], key_meta[], vs{} }

AU.name: Australia
identify: Drives on the LEFT.
White license plates with state name on top (NSW, VIC, QLD, etc.); bottom edge often has yellow trim in NSW.
Black guardrail posts with white reflectors.
Eucalyptus trees almost everywhere; reddish/dusty soil in the interior.
Yellow diamond warning signs (kangaroo, wombat, koala icons inland).

vs.NZ: AU has eucalyptus + redder soil; NZ greener with sheep + Maori-language signs.

RU.name: Russia
identify: Cyrillic alphabet, but check for unique RU letters (Ы, Э, Ъ) absent in UA/BY.
License plates: white plate, black text, blue Russian-flag strip on right with region number.
Red/white striped bollards along major roads; orange-tipped poles in colder oblasts.
Birch forests in the European center, taiga and tundra further east.
Concrete fence panels around villages are extremely common.

vs.BY: RU has Ы/Э in scripts; BY uses Belarusian Cyrillic with Ў and white-red-white motifs.
vs.UA: UA plates have a yellow strip + UA letters ЄІЇҐ; RU has the tricolor strip.

BY.name: Belarus
identify: Cyrillic with the unique letter Ў ("u-short", looks like a y with a breve).
License plates: white plate with red Belarusian flag strip on left.
Lots of birch and pine; flatter and tidier than Russia.
White or red-and-white painted concrete bollards.
Shorter signpost designs than Russia, often round white km-markers.

vs.RU: BY: Ў letter + red strip; RU: tricolor strip.

UA.name: Ukraine
identify: Cyrillic plus unique letters Є І Ї Ґ.
Plates: white with blue + yellow strip on left.
Black-and-white striped bollards in many regions.
Distinct yellow diamond rural-warning signs (Soviet legacy).
Coverage is older Gen-2 in many areas; pixelation + saturated colors.

vs.RU: UA: yellow+blue strip; RU: tricolor strip + Ы/Э.

FR.name: France
identify: License plates: long white euro-style with FR strip on left, black text, yellow rear plate.
White-painted bollards with red top reflector — very iconic.
Plane trees lining country roads (mottled bark).
Sign for street: "Rue", direction signs in white-on-blue (autoroutes) or white-on-green (national).
House numbers often on small enamel plaques.

vs.BE: FR uses red-tipped bollards; BE often has yellow road lines and 'rue/straat' bilingual signs.

DE.name: Germany
identify: Plates: white with blue EU strip on left, black text, region letters first (M, B, HH, etc.).
Bollards: white with single black diagonal stripe, sometimes reflector top.
Yellow diamond priority road sign.
Street signs are dark blue with white text, mounted on walls.
Forests are dense pine-spruce; very tidy farmland.

vs.AT: AT bollards have orange tops; signage uses Austrian phrasings (Ausfahrt vs Abfahrt).

AT.name: Austria
identify: White bollards with orange reflective top.
Plates: white with red-white-red strip.
Road signs use German with Austrian quirks (e.g., "Mautstelle" for tolls).
Mountainous terrain in the west, rolling green in the east.
Tractor + farm vehicles common on rural roads.

vs.DE: AT: orange-top bollards + RWR strip; DE: black-stripe bollards + EU strip only.

PL.name: Poland
identify: Plates: white with blue EU strip + yellow voivodeship letter (W = Warsaw, K = Krakow).
Road bollards: white with red reflector strip.
Distinctive 'A' (autostrada) and 'S' (ekspresowa) road signs in white-on-red shields.
Cyrillic-free Latin alphabet with diacritics: ą ę ł ś ż.
Gen-3 coverage with a strong antenna shadow.

vs.CZ: PL has A/S shields and ł; CZ uses D + I/D road numbering and ř.

ES.name: Spain
identify: Plates: 4 numbers + 3 letters (consonants only); ES strip on left.
Yellow-edged motorway signs in some regions; AP = peaje.
White bollards with two black strips and reflector.
Olive groves, dry scrubland in the south, deciduous forests in the north.
Town/village signs are red-bordered rectangles.

vs.PT: ES has consonant-only plate suffix; PT uses 6-char alphanumeric + region letter.

PT.name: Portugal
identify: Plates: yellow strip on right with year/month + Portuguese flag on left strip.
Cobblestone (calcada) sidewalks in towns.
Eucalyptus + cork oak in central regions.
Tile street name plaques (azulejos) in cities.
Older Gen-2 coverage in the interior — grainy + saturated.

vs.ES: PT has yellow side-strip; ES has only the EU strip on left.

BR.name: Brazil
identify: Mercosur-style plates (white with blue header) since 2018; older grey plates still common.
Blue water tanks (caixa d'água) on top of houses — iconic.
Yellow-painted curbstones in towns.
Concrete utility poles with characteristic crossbar shapes.
Portuguese-language signs (different from Spanish: ç ã õ).

vs.AR: BR speaks PT (çãõ); AR speaks ES with white plates + blue strip.

AR.name: Argentina
identify: Plates: white with black text, Mercosur header (white with blue and AR flag).
Road signs in white-on-blue with kilometer info.
Pampas grasslands in the center; Patagonia steppe in the south.
Distinctive metal-red soil in the northwest (Misiones).
Spanish with Argentine voseo (vos / tu).

vs.UY: UY has shorter, more uniform forest cover and yellow license plates with hexagonal flag.

JP.name: Japan
identify: Drives on the LEFT.
Plates: white background, green text (commercial), or yellow (kei cars), all with kanji prefecture name.
Distinctive arrow-shaped snow-direction signs in the north.
Yellow blind-pedestrian tactile paving on sidewalks.
Power poles cluttered with wires — 'spaghetti pole' meta.

vs.KR: JP has narrower roads + kanji; KR uses Hangul + wider concrete poles.

KR.name: South Korea
identify: Hangul alphabet (round + square shapes; visually distinct from kanji).
Plates: white with black text, regional Korean name on top.
Mountain hillsides extremely common; flatlands rare.
Distinct concrete utility poles with 'X' bracing pattern.
Lots of green roadside trees in summer; brown in winter.

vs.JP: KR uses Hangul + wider tan-orange highway lines; JP uses kanji + narrow road lines.

TH.name: Thailand
identify: Drives on the LEFT.
Thai script (curly, with strokes above/below baseline).
Plates: white with Thai characters + numbers; province name in Thai.
Roadside often has bright yellow + orange Buddhist shrines (sala).
Tropical vegetation; banana plants + bamboo common.

vs.VN: TH drives left + has Thai script; VN drives right + uses Vietnamese diacritics.

VN.name: Vietnam
identify: Vietnamese: Latin letters with many tone marks (áàảãạ, đ).
White plates with black text; yellow plates for commercial.
Rice paddies + conical limestone karsts in the north.
Many scooters, even in the Street View imagery.
Concrete utility poles with cylindrical transformers.

vs.TH: VN drives right + uses Latin alphabet with diacritics; TH drives left + uses Thai script.
